messages:
jamal: FYI CI microbench flagged a regression after merge to main on PR #21001 — slot-related microbench (slot_skew) jumped from ~0.9ms -> ~1.6ms (p50) for 1-token seqs. Looks like wasted time between batches (deadtime).

ci-bot: [perf] threshold-diff: microbench/slot_skew exceeded (+78%). Details: https://ci.redwood/p/21001/perf-report :link: 

sophia: on it. My quick grep showed PR touched BatchSlotAllocator::reserve() and KernelAutoselect::choose(). Might be interaction: slower slot handoff + kernel warmup. Can you paste the microbench log?

jamal: paste of the failing output:
```
# mkbench --bench slot_skew --runs 20
baseline p50: 0.92ms
current  p50: 1.63ms
histogram: baseline tight, current has a fat tail around 2.1ms
stack-sample suggests wait in BatchSlotAllocator::wait_for_slot (sleep_us path)
```

linh: I ran a local perf record and flamegraph on the CI docker image. Flamegraph snippet:
```
- wait_for_slot (45%)
  - sleep_us (30%)
  - schedule_next_batch (10%)
- kernel_select (15%)
- kv_cache_lookup (2%)
```
Looks like the allocator is doing an explicit micro-sleep when no slot is free. That used to be a non-blocking spin path with fallback — new change introduced a sleep to reduce CPU busy-waiting, but for small seqlen workloads this adds latency.

ana: (typo: ana) quick thought — for 1-token p50 we care about tail of inter-batch deadtime. Two options: revert the sleep change on hot path OR make allocator adaptive (use spin for <=N short sequences). I'm +1 for quick revert to unblock rollout.

jamal: agreed. I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up to make it adaptive. Bisect plan: revert candidate is commit 3f8a2b7 in PR #21001 -> I'll run perf CI on revert branch. If revert fixes, we'll ship hotfix.

sophia: also add a unit microbench that simulates high slot contention with short seqs so this doesn't sneak by again. mkbench test attached to PR should assert p50 < 1.1ms for 1-token workload.

ci-bot: [action] Created issue PERF-8472 and opened revert PR #21002 (run queued).
